entries.title: II Samuel 1:1
segments: ¶Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;

entries.title: II Samuel 1:2
segments: It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and [so] it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.

words.text: It came even to pass on the third
: and [so] it was, when he came

entries.title: II Samuel 1:3
segments: And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.

words.text: unto him, Out of the camp

entries.title: II Samuel 1:4
segments: And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also. {How...: Heb. What was, etc}

entries.title: II Samuel 1:5
segments: And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?

entries.title: II Samuel 1:6
segments: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:7
segments: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here [am] I. {Here...: Heb. Behold me}

entries.title: II Samuel 1:8
segments: And he said unto me, Who [art] thou? And I answered him, I [am] an Amalekite.

words.text: unto me, Who [art] thou? And I answered

entries.title: II Samuel 1:9
segments: He said unto me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life [is] yet whole in me. {anguish...: or, my coat of mail (or, my embroidered coat) hindereth me, that my, etc}

words.text: , I pray thee, upon me, and slay
[is] yet whole in me. {anguish...: or, my coat of mail (or, my embroidered coat) hindereth me, that my, etc}

entries.title: II Samuel 1:10
segments: So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that [was] upon his head, and the bracelet that [was] on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:11
segments: ¶Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that [were] with him:

words.text: them; and likewise all the men

entries.title: II Samuel 1:12
segments: And they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:13
segments: And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence [art] thou? And he answered, I [am] the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.

words.text: him, Whence [art] thou? And he answered

entries.title: II Samuel 1:14
segments: And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the LORD'S anointed?

words.text: unto him, How wast thou not afraid

entries.title: II Samuel 1:15
segments: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, [and] fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:16
segments: And David said unto him, Thy blood [be] upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the LORD'S anointed.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:17
segments: ¶And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son:

entries.title: II Samuel 1:18
segments: (Also he bade them teach the children of Judah [the use of] the bow: behold, [it is] written in the book of Jasher.) {of Jasher: or, of the upright}

entries.title: II Samuel 1:19
segments: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!

entries.title: II Samuel 1:20
segments: Tell [it] not in Gath, publish [it] not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:21
segments: Ye mountains of Gilboa, [let there be] no dew, neither [let there be] rain, upon you, nor fields of offerings: for there the shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, [as though he had] not [been] anointed with oil.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:22
segments: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:23
segments: Saul and Jonathan [were] lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions. {pleasant: or, sweet}

entries.title: II Samuel 1:24
segments: Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with [other] delights, who put on ornaments of gold upon your apparel.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:25
segments: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, [thou wast] slain in thine high places.

entries.title: II Samuel 1:26
segments: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.

words.text: hast thou been unto me: thy love

entries.title: II Samuel 1:27
segments: How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!
